title: The transport uploads files in chunks and, on the tus.io branch, exposes an Upload-Offset header per PATCH
asA: operator uploading a large file over a spotty connection
iWant: the transport to split my file into chunks and to resume from the last acknowledged offset on retry
soThat: an interrupted upload does not re-send bytes I already delivered

acceptanceCriteria.description: On the ?transport=multipart branch the fixture returns 200 with a completed chunk count higher than 1 on a file large enough to force chunking; the DOM exposes [data-transport="multipart"] and [data-chunks-uploaded] whose numeric value equals the completed chunk count. On the ?transport=tus branch the pack observes at least one PATCH request on the browser's network log whose request headers include Upload-Offset with a numeric value, and the DOM exposes [data-transport="tus"] with [data-chunks-uploaded] > 1.

When the transport is tus.io and no tus server or client library prerequisite is available at apply time, apply refuses with TUS_PREREQUISITE_MISSING naming the missing side (server or client) and the remedy to install it; no upload code is written to the project until the prerequisite is present.
acceptanceCriteria.given: tus transport elicited without the tus server or client dependency installed
acceptanceCriteria.then: apply exits with a non-zero code, TUS_PREREQUISITE_MISSING names the missing side and the remedy, and no transport code is added

acceptanceCriteria.description: Upload-Offset on the tus branch matches the byte offset the server has durably acknowledged; a chunk write that returns a non-2xx does not advance Upload-Offset and a subsequent PATCH resumes from the last acknowledged offset.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a tus upload with a chunk that returns a non-2xx
acceptanceCriteria.when: the client inspects Upload-Offset and retries
acceptanceCriteria.then: Upload-Offset reflects the last acknowledged offset only, and the resume PATCH sends bytes from that offset onward

acceptanceCriteria.description: A chunk write whose response body does not include a valid Upload-Offset header (missing, malformed, or beyond the total) is treated as a transport failure: the client refuses to advance and the polite live region announces the failure.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a chunk response with a malformed or missing Upload-Offset
acceptanceCriteria.then: the client does not advance its offset, the polite live region announces the failure and a retry stays keyboard-reachable
